turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Good afternoon, thanks for calling Acme Life, this is Ethan speaking. Just so you know, this call is recorded for quality and training purposes. How can I help you today?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Hi Ethan. I saw your ad for term life with no medical exam. I've got maybe ten minutes between meetings, so if we can keep this quick, that'd be great.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Absolutely, I'll keep it efficient. Before we get into any details or a quote, can I get your full name and date of birth, please?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Olivia Roy. March 14th, 1986.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Thanks, Olivia. That's Olivia Roy, born March 14th, 1986. Is that right?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Yep, that's me.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Great. So I can point you to the right amount of cover, could you tell me a bit about your situation and what's prompting you to look at life insurance?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Can't you just give me a price? Okay, fine. Short version: I run a small bakery, I've got two kids, eight and eleven, and a mortgage. My partner works part-time. If something happened to me, I don't want them losing the house.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: That's really helpful, thank you. Roughly how much is left on the mortgage, and do you have any life cover already, through the business or anywhere else?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: About $380,000 left on the mortgage. No other coverage. I keep meaning to sort it out, which is why I'm calling.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Understood. And how long until the mortgage is paid off, roughly?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Around nineteen years.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Okay. Here's a quick overview of how Acme Term Life works. You can choose cover anywhere from $50,000 up to $750,000. Terms are either 10 or 20 years, and your premium stays fixed for the whole term. There's no medical exam; acceptance depends on a few health questions. A couple of things to be aware of: it's pure protection, so there's no cash value and nothing paid back if you outlive the term. And you get a 30-day free-look period, so if you change your mind within 30 days you get a full refund.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Okay. So what would you suggest?

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Given the mortgage at about $380,000, nineteen years to go, and two kids, a 20-year term lines up well with the mortgage. In terms of amount, something like $500,000 would clear the mortgage and leave a cushion for your partner and the kids. That said, it's your call. You could go closer to the mortgage balance if you'd rather keep the cost down.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: $500,000 for 20 years sounds about right. What's that going to cost me?

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: I'll need to run through the health questions first, since that determines acceptance and the price. There are just a few. Have you smoked or used any nicotine products in the last twelve months?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: No, never smoked.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: In the past five years, have you been diagnosed with or treated for heart disease, cancer, stroke or diabetes?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: No.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Are you currently waiting on any medical tests or results, or have you been hospitalized in the last two years?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: No, nothing like that. Just the odd sinus infection.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: That's fine, that doesn't affect anything. Based on your answers, you're eligible, and for $500,000 over a 20-year term your premium would be $80 a month, fixed for the full 20 years.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Eighty a month. Hmm. Is that the best you can do? I was kind of hoping for less.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: That's the rate for that amount and term. If you wanted to bring it down, a lower amount, say closer to the $380,000 mortgage, or a 10-year term would cost less. Though a 10-year term would end well before the mortgage is paid off. Would you like me to quote any of those?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: No, the 20 years matters to me. I just like to ask. Okay, let's just do it. Where do I sign?

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: No rush at all on my end. If you'd prefer to talk it over with your partner first, I can email you the quote and you can come back to it whenever suits you.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: No, we already talked about it last week. I'd rather just get it done today while I'm thinking about it.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Sounds good. Let me just summarize before we finalize. This is Acme Term Life, $500,000 of coverage over a 20-year term, at $80 a month, and that premium is fixed for the full 20 years. There's no cash value, so if you outlive the term nothing is paid out. You have a 30-day free-look period with a full refund if you change your mind. Do you want to go ahead with this policy?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Yes, I want to go ahead.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Perfect. I'll take your banking details for the monthly payment, then send your policy documents by email, which will include the details on the free-look period. Shall we do the payment details now?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Yes, go ahead. Quickly, though, I've got a supplier calling at quarter past.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Understood, it'll only take a couple of minutes. Thanks for your patience, Olivia.
